__comment: Nextcloud, ownCloud and any WebDAV server (a NAS, Apache mod_dav, rclone, ...). No OAuth: the customUI app com.palm.app.webdav-auth collects the server type, address, user name and password (an app password for Nextcloud/ownCloud) and calls com.palm.service.webdav/login, which finds the user's WebDAV folder, checks the sign-in with a PROPFIND and returns the stored credentials. Provides BOTH DOCUMENTS and PHOTO.UPLOAD.
__comment2: com.palm.app.webdav-auth MUST be in write/readPermissions: createAccount runs under the customUI auth app's identity and is permission-checked against these lists.
__comment3: com.palm.service.webdav is in read+writePermissions so the service can readCredentials(accountId) for file ops. A password does not expire, so the service does not normally write back, but the permission is kept for symmetry.

capabilityProviders.__comment: The Documents app, Topaz Explorer's cloud drives and the account-derived QuickOffice reroute consume listFolder/downloadFile/uploadFile/createFolder/moveItem/deleteItem. Locators are paths under the account's WebDAV folder ('/' is that folder; a folder's path ends in '/').

Makes the account a photo source. The Photos aggregator calls com.palm.service.webdav/listAlbums+listPhotos: the photo folder ('Photos' unless the account names another) and each folder in it are albums. WebDAV wants the password on every request, so listPhotos downloads each photo to /media/internal/.webdav-photos and hands file:// links (temporary:true), as MEGA does.
